verses.96:2: Nuvem e {caligo} estão ao seu redor: * justiça e juízo são {correctio} do seu trono.
verses.96:3: Um fogo {praecedet}, * e {inflammabit} ao redor os seus inimigos.
verses.96:4: Os seus relâmpagos iluminaram o mundo: * a terra viu, e se abalou.
verses.96:6: Os céus anunciaram a sua justiça: * e todos os povos viram a sua glória.
verses.96:7: {confundantur} todos os que adoram {sculptilia}: * e os que se gloriam nos seus {simulacra}.
verses.96:8: {exsultaverunt}, * por causa dos vossos juízos, Senhor:
verses.96:9: Porque vós sois o Senhor altíssimo sobre toda a terra: * sois {nimis} todos os deuses.

verses.96:11: {lux} para o justo, * e a alegria para os retos de coração.

decisions.why: The formula opens Pss 92, 96 and 98. Ps 92 ruled the Latin's perfect (*O Senhor reinou*, following the Greek aorist ἐβασίλευσεν; DRB 'hath reigned', MS1932 *é rei* here but *reinou* at 92:1) and asked Pss 96 and 98 to open the same way (glossary row 92:1a). Copied.

options.label: reinou
options.note: the Latin's perfect; the Ps 92 formula

options.label: é rei
options.note: MS1932 at this verse: the state, not the act; interprets the aorist

options.label: reina
options.note: the Hebrew family's present; the Latin does not say it

decisions.why: *multæ* is a plain 'many'; the Latin has no article. *as muitas ilhas* is the plain word in natural order; MS1932 has *as numerosas ilhas*. Without the article (*alegrem-se muitas ilhas*) Portuguese hears 'a good number of islands (but not all)', a restriction the Latin does not make. v2: the stylist heard *as muitas ilhas* as a calque, flat at the final cadence, and asked *as ilhas numerosas* — the same 'many', natural order and a paroxytone close; taken under D2.

options.label: as ilhas numerosas
options.note: v2 — the stylist's: adjective after the noun (as muitas ilhas sounded translated and flat at the cadence); same sense, a matter of how it is said (D2)

options.label: as muitas ilhas
options.note: draft — the plainer of two faithful words

options.label: muitas ilhas
options.note: no article, as the Latin; heard as 'a number of islands'

decisions.why: The glossary row *calígo → névoa escura* (17:10, γνόφος — the same Greek here) named this verse as its next place, beside *nubes → nuvem*. *trevas* is *ténebræ*'s; *escuridão* (MS1932) is plainer but loses the mist the Latin word holds. *Nubes* is singular in the Latin and stays so.

options.label: névoa escura
options.note: the glossary row (17:10)

options.label: escuridão
options.note: MS1932; plainer, loses the mist

options.label: treva
options.note: collides with ténebræ → trevas

decisions.why: *Corréctio* is the Latin's calque of κατόρθωσις, 'a setting upright, establishment' (DRB 'the establishment of his throne'); Lewis & Short has only 'amendment, correction'. The cognate *correção* would be heard as the throne being corrected — a wrong first hearing. *firmeza* keeps the upright, established throne without interpreting it into a building part; *base* (MS1932) turns it into a foundation (that is 88:15's *præparátio*, and the Hebrew's מְכוֹן). *retidão* is taken by *diréctio*. The v2 Latinist (minor) found *firmeza* a static quality for a noun of action and asked *estabelecimento* (or *retidão*); refused — *estabelecimento* is heard as a shop, *retidão* is diréctio's. *firmeza* stays; the options are there.

options.label: a firmeza
options.note: draft — the throne set upright and established (κατόρθωσις)

options.label: a base
options.note: MS1932; a foundation — nearer the Hebrew's 'foundation'

options.label: o aprumo
options.note: the literal 'uprightness'; in current speech 'poise, elegance'

options.label: a correção
options.note: the cognate; heard as correcting the throne

options.label: o estabelecimento
options.note: Latinist v2 (minor): the noun of action (κατόρθωσις). Refused: in Brazil *estabelecimento* is first a shop or business

decisions.why: The Ps 87 agent proposed *preceder* for the friendly transitive *præveníre* (87:14 *a minha oração vos precederá*; 58:10 to follow) and flagged that *præcédere* here would then need another word. *Ir adiante de* is the plain Portuguese for 'go before', is the Greek (πῦρ ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ προπορεύσεται) and is MS1932's wording (*O fogo irá adiante dele*); it absorbs the Latin's *ante ipsum* + *præ-* in one phrase. 88:15 *præcédent fáciem tuam* has the same Greek verb and should follow (*irão adiante da vossa face*). 84:14 *Justítia ante eum ambulábit* is the same Greek phrase but another Latin verb, and keeps its *andará diante dele*.

options.label: irá adiante dele
options.note: draft — MS1932; leaves preceder to præveníre

options.label: andará diante dele
options.note: 84:14's wording for the same Greek phrase; but that is ambuláre

options.label: o precederá
options.note: the cognate; collides with the Ps 87 proposal for præveníre

decisions.latin: et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos ejus
decisions.why: The fire sets the enemies aflame (φλογιεῖ). The cognate *inflamará* is used for a heart catching fire at 72:21 (another Greek verb), but with persons as object current Portuguese hears 'stir them up' or a medical inflammation. *abrasar* is the fire's own verb (MS1932), *queimar* the plainest. v2: the ambiguity reader listed *abrasará* as unknown and warned it is heard as *abraçará* ('will embrace') — a wrong first hearing, so the plain verb is taken; the fire is still the subject, so the burning is still a flame's.

options.label: queimará
options.note: v2 — plainest; DRB 'shall burn'. Taken after the ambiguity reader listed abrasará as unknown and heard it as abraçará ('will embrace')

options.label: abrasará
options.note: draft 1 — MS1932; keeps the flame, but unknown to the ambiguity reader and misheard as abraçará

options.label: inflamará
options.note: the cognate (72:21 se inflamou); with persons heard as 'stir up'

decisions.latin: Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini
decisions.why: The row *flúere → escorrer* (57:9 *como a cera que escorre*; 67:3 *como escorre a cera à face do fogo*) and *a fácie → à face de* (Ps 67, seven times, the same melting-wax image) are applied, so the three wax verses of the psalter say the same thing. The Greek has 'melted' (ἐτάκησαν; MS1932 *fundiram-se*), but the Latin says 'flowed'. The repetition *a fácie Dómini … a fácie Dómini* is kept. The Latinist (v1, minor) asked *diante da face*; refused for 67:3's sake, option. The ambiguity reader heard the second colon as a verbless statement (the earth is before the Lord) — which is how the Latin's ellipsis also reads; kept (decision `omnisterra`).

options.label: escorreram à face do Senhor
options.note: draft — the rows of 57:9 and 67:3

options.label: derreteram-se diante do Senhor
options.note: the Greek's verb (MS1932 fundiram-se … diante do Senhor); the face lost

options.label: escorreram diante da face do Senhor
options.note: Latinist v1 (minor): 'a facie' is 'from before / at the presence of'; refused to keep the three wax verses one (67:3 à face do fogo … à face de Deus, which passed the Latinist twice) and because it adds 4 syllables to each colon

decisions.why: The Latin's *omnis terra* is nominative: 'before the face of the Lord, all the earth [flowed]' — the verb is carried over from the first colon. The Greek reads a genitive, 'the Lord of all the earth' (DRB follows it); MS1932 supplies a verb (*se funde toda a terra*). The Latin's ellipsis is kept, which leaves the verb to be heard from the first colon as the Latin does; supplying *escorreu* would be allowed as grammar, but the bare colon is sayable and keeps the echo clean.

options.label: toda a terra (ellipsis)
options.note: draft — the Latin's ellipsis

options.label: escorreu toda a terra
options.note: the verb supplied (MS1932 supplies one)

options.label: do Senhor de toda a terra
options.note: the Greek's genitive, DRB; not the Latin

decisions.why: *confúndi → ser envergonhado* is settled (D15), and the jussive *Confundántur* is *Sejam envergonhados* at 34:4. The stylist (v1) found the periphrastic passive heavy in an already long colon and asked for the pronominal *Envergonhem-se*. Refused for the row (passive voice is the Latin's, and the formula recurs); kept as an option — it would save two syllables here.

options.label: Envergonhem-se
options.note: stylist v1: lighter; the pronominal for the passive

decisions.why: 77:58 *in sculptílibus suis* → *com as suas imagens esculpidas*; copied. The colon runs long (~+5 syllables) for it; *esculturas* is shorter but is heard as works of art, *ídolos* is needed for *simulácra* in the next colon.

options.label: esculturas
options.note: shorter; heard as art

options.label: ídolos
options.note: MS1932; merges with simulácra in the next colon

decisions.why: First place of *simulácrum* (εἴδωλον; 113:12 = 134:15 *Simulácra géntium* to come). The cognate *simulacros* (MS1932) is bookish and would need a footnote; *ídolos* is the Greek's word and the plain one. Proposed as a new glossary row. The stylist (v1) disliked the proparoxytone close *ídolos* and asked *simulacros*; refused — bookish (it would need a footnote, rule 5); the proparoxytone is accepted (the cadence tolerates it; *ídolos* is the plain word).

options.label: ídolos
options.note: draft — εἴδωλα; DRB 'idols'

options.label: simulacros
options.note: MS1932; the cognate, bookish

decisions.why: The Latin puts *Sion* last, after both verbs. Coming straight after *Adorai-o … anjos*, a verse-initial *ouviu* leaves the ear asking who heard; the subject is moved to the head (natural order, D2). The Latin's order is an option.

The stylist (v1) heard the vowel clash *E ex-* at the head of a verse as a stumble in choir and asked for the subject first. Order only (D2); taken. The mediant now falls on *exultaram* (paroxytone).

decisions.why: The *nimis* row has no single rendering. The nearest formula, *laudábilis nimis* (47:2 = 95:4), is settled (D43) as *muito digno de louvor*; 95:4 stands two verses before this in the Office. *muito* keeps that; *sem medida* (118:138) is closer to 'beyond measure' but adds three syllables. The stylist (v1) found *muito exaltado* colloquial and asked *exaltado muito acima de*; refused (the Latin's *super … super* repetition), kept as an option; *sem medida* remains the answer if Gustavo also hears it as weak.

options.label: muito exaltado sobre
options.note: draft — as 47:2 = 95:4 (D43); super … super kept

options.label: exaltado sem medida sobre
options.note: 118:138; 'beyond measure'

options.label: exaltado muito acima de
options.note: stylist v1: 'muito exaltado' colloquial and weak. Refused: acima de for super dissolves the Latin's super … super

decisions.why: The row *oríri → nascer* (71:7; 84:12 *A verdade nasceu da terra*) names this verse. ἀνέτειλεν is the rising of a star; *nascer* is what the sun does in Portuguese (*o sol nasce*), so the image holds. Subject first, as 84:12; MS1932 has *Nasceu a luz para os justos*.

options.label: A luz nasceu
options.note: the oríri row; subject first as 84:12

options.label: Nasceu a luz
options.note: MS1932's order

decisions.why: 29:5 has *confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus* → *dai graças à memória da sua santidade*, and its row says 96:12 should copy the colon 'with its own noun'. But the Greek of both is one word, τῆς ἁγιωσύνης αὐτοῦ (checked in consult/parallels/ps029.md and ps096.md): by D15's test the Latin's variation carries no sense to keep, and DRB says 'holiness' in both. *santificação* would say an act of making holy, which ἁγιωσύνη is not. (95:6 *in sanctificatióne ejus* is ἁγίασμα, the sanctuary — another sense; Ps 95 decides it.) The Latinist (v1, minor) asked *santificação* as the verbal noun; refused on the Greek (ἁγιωσύνη, the quality, both here and at 29:5 — the Latin's variation is Jerome's, not a second sense). The ambiguity reader heard the Lord's holiness first (a faint papal echo in *sua santidade*, which 29:5 shares). The v2 gate asked *santificação* again (minor, conceding *santidade* is the sense); held for the same reason.

options.label: santidade
options.note: draft — one Greek word with 29:5; the colon identical to 29:5b

options.label: santificação
options.note: the cognate; the Latin's own noun kept apart from 29:5; heard as the act of sanctifying

choices.96:1: *exsúltet / læténtur → exulte / alegrem-se* (the exsultáre / lætári row).
choices.96:2: Both copulas supplied (the Latin is verbless in both colons), as 92:2. *in circúitu ejus → ao seu redor* (75:12's form). *sedes → trono* (the row).
choices.96:3: *Ignis* without article → *Um fogo* (as 38:4 *um fogo se inflamará*); MS1932 *O fogo*. *in circúitu → ao redor* with no object, as 11:9. v2: *abrasará → queimará* (decision `inflammabit`).
choices.96:4: Copies 76:19 *Os vossos relâmpagos iluminaram o mundo: * a terra se abalou e estremeceu*: *fúlgura* here and *coruscatiónes* there are one Greek word (ἀστραπαί), so one Portuguese word (D15; 17:15 *relâmpagos* for *fúlgura* too). *orbis terræ → o mundo* (D30). *commóta est → se abalou* (76:19, 17:8). Subject named first in the second colon (natural order).
choices.96:7: *Confundántur → Sejam envergonhados* (D15; 34:4). The first colon runs long for *imagens esculpidas* (see decision). *gloriári in → gloriar-se em*: the row kept the verb for exactly this place (sinners' boasting).
choices.96:7b: *ángelus → anjo*, lowercase. *Adorai-o* is safe under rule 3 (past *adorei*). Draft 1 had *Adorai-o, vós, todos os seus anjos* (the 29:5 / 30:24 build); the stylist (v1) found the inserted *vós* a stumble that blurs the address in a psalm where God is *vós*. Taken in v2: here the object *-o* is already expressed, so *todos os seus anjos* can only be the vocative — the reason *vós* was supplied at 29:5 and 30:24 (a bare noun that could be heard as the object) does not apply. The line is quoted at Heb 1:6.
choices.96:8: Second colon identical to 47:12b (*por causa dos vossos juízos, Senhor*); *exsultáre → exultar* as 47:12a. The psalm turns to address the Lord here (*tua*), so *vossos*.
choices.96:9: *tu Dóminus Altíssimus → vós sois o Senhor altíssimo*: copula supplied; lowercase adjective as 7:18 (*altíssimo Senhor*), after the noun here because the colon's cadence is on *terra*. *super … super → sobre … sobre*, the Latin's repetition kept.
choices.96:10: *odíte → odiai* (safe: past *odiei*). *Vós que amais* names the plural humans (D1, Ps 10:2 remedy) — the Lord is in the third person here, so no confusion with the address of 96:8–9. *sanctus (ὅσιος) → santo*; *peccátor* singular kept.
choices.96:11: *justo* singular kept (MS1932 pluralizes). *rectus corde → reto de coração* (the row). Order: *e a alegria para os retos de coração* — the Latin ends on *lætítia*; the natural order closes on the oxytone *coração*.
choices.96:12: *Lætámini, justi, in Dómino* in the Latin's order with *ó* before the vocative (31:11, 32:1 have *ó justos*). *confitéri → dar graças a* (D5). Second colon = 29:5b.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps096.md (no DM1962 section for this psalm) and the glossary. Rows applied: Dóminus regnávit (92:1a), exsultáre/lætári, calígo (17:10), in circúitu (75:12), sedes, orbis terræ (D30), commovére (76:19), flúere (57:9, 67:3), a fácie (67), confúndi (D15), gloriári in, sculptília (77:58), ángelus, 47:12b, Altíssimus, nimis (47:2, D43), odísse, custodíre, liberáre, sanctus, peccátor, oríri (84:12), rectus corde, confitéri (D5), memória / 29:5b. Hard readings: *corréctio sedis* (κατόρθωσις), *a fácie Dómini omnis terra* (nominative in the Latin, genitive in the Greek), *præcédere* against the Ps 87 proposal for *præveníre*, *sanctificátio* = ἁγιωσύνη as 29:5's *sánctitas*.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 96:7 first colon +7 (imagens esculpidas, 77:58's term; still one breath — esculturas, −3, is an option); 96:11 +3 / +6 (the Latin is at its tersest; Portuguese needs articles and prepositions for the two datives); 96:2 first colon +3 (copula supplied in a verbless Latin colon, as 92:2); 96:10 second colon −5 and 96:12 second colon −4 (Latin polysyllables against Portuguese elisions). No rhyme flags.
